title: Carolyn Groobey (NACD Directorship 100) on the keynote's opening line — 'Why are boards terrible?'
summary: Groobey is a lead independent director named to the 2026 NACD Directorship 100. Her post on LinkedIn called the NACD Summit the Hamilton of governance conferences and reported Eric's keynote as the session she left humming, tying it to her board service at VHB, an employee-owned firm.
blockquote: This year, mine came from Eric Ries, who opened with a question you don’t often hear at a governance conference: “Why are boards terrible?” His argument, from his new book Incorruptible: boards that break from “best practices” often outperform, because they stay anchored to mission and values and think in decades, not quarters.
